subject: Re: weighting global density estimate in model definition

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: weighting global density estimate in model definition
parts:
> > I have two geographic regions and would like to stratify via the stratum
> > data layer to get density estimates for both. In the "Model Definition
> > Properties" "Estimate" tab, I am unclear how to weight my global density
> > estimate. My area for each region is zero (from the area field in the data
> > explorer). The F1 help menu says to use the default settings for geographic
> > stratification, but there is no picture so I am unsure as to what weighting
> > is appropriate. Weighting by area gives a higher density estimate than
> > giving equal weighting to all strata, even though the area is set to zero.
> > My gut feeling is that I should give equal weight to all strata, because I
> > have eight transects of equal length in each region.

As Len is on holiday, I'll respond briefly - as I'm not sure what Distance
does in this circumstance, he might clarify once he is back.

First, I'm puzzled why you have set your areas to zero. Second, if you
want global density, it should be

(total number of animals in popn)/(total area)

The number of transects you have in each stratum has nothing to do with
this. But you can only get a valid estimate of this density if you have
transects randomly positioned in each stratum (or a randomly-positioned
grid of transects). The no. (and length) of transects in each stratum
affects precision, but not weighting.

When strata are geographic, you get the global density by taking a
weighted average of stratum densities, where weights are stratum
areas. If you don't give any stratum areas, I'm not sure what the default
is - I would have guessed it is to weight by total effort in each stratum,
which is fine provided line length per stratum is proportional to stratum
size. In your case, this should be the same as giving equal weighting to
each stratum estimate, but your results show it is not doing that. Note
that, for geographic strata, you must take the global density estimate as
the mean, not the sum, of the stratum estimates - I assume you're doing
that?

The simple solution is to give Distance the appropriate stratum areas -
and if you can't, it is because you don't have well-defined geographic
strata, so that a global density is not well-defined. In that case, I
would just get the stratum density estimates, and not seek to get a global
estimate.

Steve Buckland
